title: Optimal propagation has value one
statement: Let $q$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a finite unique game with a nonempty set of variables and a nonempty set of constraints. Each constraint joins two distinct variables, carries a permutation of the $q$ labels, and every variable occurs in some constraint. If the optimum value of the associated constraint satisfaction instance is $1$, then the assignment obtained by propagating the selected labels from component roots has value $1$.
hypotheses_covered: The variable set is finite and nonempty
The constraint set is finite and nonempty
Each constraint carries a permutation of the labels
Every variable participates in a constraint
The associated constraint satisfaction instance has optimum $1$
